candidates: TETHER LOCK: Hold your aim on a drifting target to fill a lock ring; swinging onto a different target mid-hold cancels the ring and forces you to restart, so you must commit to one target at a time.

CROSSWIRE CONVERGE: Two independently controlled crosshairs must overlap on the same target at once to fire; the player decides how to time and route each axis into alignment before the target moves away.
RICOCHET LINE: Drag back and release to launch a bouncing shot whose angle and power you set; the player decides the bounce path needed to chain through multiple targets off the arena walls.
GRID RESERVE: Breaking small nodes banks charge that is spent unlocking rarer high-value nodes; the player decides when to bank versus when to spend accumulated charge.
FREQ SWITCH: Targets arrive tagged with one of three signal frequencies and the player must select the matching weapon mode before firing, or the shot is wasted and the combo resets.

SPLIT SWARM: Shooting a target splits it into two smaller, faster targets worth less each; the player decides whether to keep splitting for volume or leave clusters alone to avoid getting overwhelmed.

GRAVITY SNARE: Clicking places a pulsing attractor field that pulls nearby drifting targets toward a collection point; the player decides where and when to place the limited-duration field rather than clicking targets directly.
ECHO SEQUENCE: A short flash sequence of positions lights up and the player must click them back in the same order before it fades, with sequences growing longer over time.
TRIP LINE: Dragging draws a limited-length wire across the arena that destroys anything crossing it while active; the player decides where to place each use of a shared, regenerating length budget.
SURGE WAIT: Targets grow in value the longer they are left unshot but can overload and vanish if left too long; the player decides how long to let each one ride before cashing it in.
DUAL WATCH: Two separate lanes each need defending but only one turret can be active at a time; the player decides when to swap control between lanes, leaving the other briefly undefended.
PING REVEAL: Clicking sends a pulse that briefly reveals nearby hidden targets in a radius; the player decides where to ping and which revealed targets to hit before they fade back to invisible.
reason: TETHER LOCK scored highest overall on stability and immediate feedback (a visibly filling lock ring each frame you hold) while introducing a decision axis no existing work uses — sustained commitment with a real switching cost — and it maps cleanly onto mouse-hold, touch-hold, and keyboard-hold controls without extra complexity.
